CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow up of chronic problems.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Anna is a 44-year-old female with past medical history of arthritis, gout, and reflux presenting for follow up of her chronic conditions. She reports that her arthritis has been improving with exercise including pilates and weight lifting, which has helped build muscle and reduce joint pain. She completed physical therapy for her right knee and is now able to walk 1 to 1.5 miles daily. She had a gout flare involving her right first metatarsophalangeal joint approximately two months ago which resolved with medication. She is compliant with allopurinol. Regarding her reflux, she reports starting dietary modifications but has not completely eliminated certain foods. She continues to experience morning vomiting and nausea despite omeprazole therapy. She also reports abdominal pain and bloating. Her last bowel movement was two days ago and was normal without blood. She denies weight loss, fever, or chills.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and abdominal distension. Negative for diarrhea, weight loss, fever, and chills.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Arthritis, gout, reflux.

MEDICATIONS
Omeprazole 40 mg once daily, allopurinol 100 mg once daily.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Exercises regularly with pilates and weight lifting.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs are stable. Heart sounds normal. Lungs clear to auscultation. Abdomen: pain to palpation in right upper quadrant, no rebound or guarding, no peritoneal signs. Right knee: mild effusion, mild pain to palpation, decreased range of motion.

RESULTS
Autoimmune panel: normal. Right knee X-ray: no fracture, residual arthritis.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Reflux, nausea, and vomiting: Continue omeprazole 40 mg once daily. Continue dietary modifications. Obtain right upper quadrant ultrasound to rule out gallstones. Check labs.

2. Gout: Well controlled. Continue allopurinol 100 mg once daily. Refill ordered.

3. Arthritis: Significant improvement noted. Continue pilates and knee use. Follow up regarding any issues and discuss further imaging or intervention as needed.
